title: IPC admin.trust.list result
description: One page of the profile's data-plane allowlist as `PeerTrustPolicy` holds it (2.1): the allowed peers, ascending by canonical string, at most 1024 a page, on a connection that negotiated 2.3 or later `persisted: true` on every row with its `source` — `configured` for a peer `config.yaml` lists, `administered` for one added over `admin.trust.set` and kept in the state directory's trust overlay (ADR-0028 A 2026-10-07) — and below 2.3 the 2.1 row, `persisted: false` and no `source` (1.0.0 described only that row; 1.1.0 widens it behind the minor under ADR-0017 A 2026-10-07: a closed result shape widens behind a new minor while the old shape is served below it); `next` is the last row's peer when more remain and absent on the last page; `local_peer`, this profile's own identity, is on the first page only and absent when the policy has none. Every peer not listed is denied: deny-by-default is the policy's shape, not a setting, so there is no default here and no per-peer decision, which is a local diagnostic (ADR-0032). A page of 1024 rows is about 105 KiB as 2.3 rows (105 bytes a row with its comma, for a 52-character peer id; 82 KiB as 2.1 rows), under the 128 KiB body. architect-cto's ruling of 2026-10-04 (relay message 01a10820-b85d-74e6-bf40-e23b46c77a82). AN ENDPOINT ANSWER (IPC 3.0, ADR-0067 decision 6, LOCAL-IPC.md §The endpoint dimension, 1.2.0): the answer to `admin.trust.list {endpoint, direction}` carries `set` — `own` (the endpoint's overlay set: every row `administered` and `persisted: true`), `authored` (an authored `static_subset`: rows `configured`) or `inherited` (the operator's rows, with their own sources) — and has no `local_peer`; `set` is present only on an endpoint answer, so its presence is what tells an endpoint answer from the operator's.

persisted.description: false on a connection below 2.3 (the 2.1 row); true on 2.3 and later: every row survives a daemon restart, configured rows by config.yaml, administered rows by the state directory's trust overlay (ADR-0028 A 2026-10-07).

source.description: On 2.3 and later only, where the row comes from: `config.yaml`'s trust.allowed_peers, or an `admin.trust.set` kept in the trust overlay. A configured peer revoked over IPC is not listed; a normalised overlay has no peer in both.

items.description: The 2.1 row (persisted false, no source) below minor 2.3; the 2.3 row (persisted true with source) on 2.3 and later (ADR-0017 A 2026-10-07).

allowed.description: Unique by peer and strictly ascending; JSON Schema cannot state the order, the Rust mirror refuses a page that breaks it.

set.description: Present only on an endpoint answer: which set the page is of. `own` rows are all `administered` and `persisted: true`.

set.$comment: An endpoint answer has no local_peer (LOCAL-IPC.md, The endpoint dimension). The converse, that set is on every endpoint answer, is not a property of the document alone, since the result does not say whether the request named an endpoint: the Rust side's one endpoint constructor, TrustList::page_endpoint, always sets it.
